findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new flexbox mixin set is internally inconsistent: flexbox() emits display:-moz-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group, but align-items() omits the matching -moz-box-align and instead emits -ms-align-items, a property no browser has ever implemented. Browsers that resolve to the 2009 box display (Firefox <=21) get a flex container from flexbox() but no alignment declaration, so .d-header .contents and .badge-wrapper.bullet fall back to the box-align default (stretch) instead of the intended center/baseline; every align-items() call site also ships the inert -ms-align-items declaration into the compiled CSS, and the unverified prefix list is exactly the drift this hand-maintained enumeration is supposed to prevent.

[BUG] `.panel` swaps `float: right` for `margin-left: auto`, but auto-margin alignment does not exist in the old flexbox syntaxes the new mixins deliberately emit (`display: -ms-flexbox`, `-webkit-box`, `-moz-box` in mixins.scss), so on those browsers the panel is never pushed to the header's right edge. In IE10 (where `-ms-flexbox` is the only recognized display value from the mixin) and old-spec-only WebKit/Firefox builds, `.panel` renders immediately after the title in the flex row instead of pinned right, stranding the search/avatar/login controls mid-header; the mixin file's own `-ms-flexbox`/`-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` lines declare these browsers in the intended support set, so the layout technique contradicts the fallback matrix the same PR ships.

[BUG] `.extra-info-wrapper` becomes a flex item of the now-flexible `.contents` with the default `min-width: auto` in a single-line (no `flex-wrap`) row, so its minimum width is pinned to the full rendered width of the topic title it contains and the row cannot shrink it. For a long topic title, or a title containing a long unbroken word/URL (common in pasted-link titles), the wrapper's min-content width exceeds the space beside the logo and panel; the flex row overflows and `.panel` is pushed past the header's right edge and clipped, whereas the deleted float layout let the title block occupy only the space between the floats and wrap/ellipsize there. The same min-width exposure applies to the `.title` flex item for long text-only site titles.

[BUG] The float declarations that produced the header layout (`float: left` on `.title`, `float: right` on `.panel`) are deleted rather than retained ahead of the flex declarations, so a browser that recognizes none of the five `display` values emitted by `flexbox()` falls back to block layout with nothing positioning the children horizontally. On browsers with no flexbox support at all (IE9, Opera Mini), the logo, topic title, and panel stack vertically inside the fixed-height header and the panel is clipped out of view; the sibling conversion in topic-post.scss keeps the base `.topic-avatar { float: left }` rule so `.small-action` still degrades to the float layout, showing the header conversion dropped the fallback its sibling kept — retaining the floats before `@include flexbox()` is the standard no-cost fix since floats are ignored on flex items.

[ADVISORY] The new `align-items` mixin violates the SCSS lint rules the repo gates on: `align-items:$alignment;` has no space after the colon (SpaceAfterColon), the `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` line carries trailing whitespace (TrailingWhitespace), and the mixin body is indented 4 spaces against the file's 2-space style (Indentation). The repo's scss-lint run fails on this file, and since a CSS-only diff ships no other automated verification (no spec/test/visual-regression files anywhere in the diff), the change either lands with its only check red or the lint configuration gets weakened to admit it.

[ADVISORY] `align-items()` forwards `$alignment` verbatim into the old-spec properties, but `flex-start`/`flex-end` — the most common align-items values — are invalid in the 2009/2011 syntaxes (`-webkit-box-align`/`-ms-flex-align` require `start`/`end`), and the mixin also emits the non-existent property `-ms-align-items`. The next call site that passes `flex-start` or `flex-end` gets silently wrong vertical alignment on exactly the legacy browsers the mixin exists to support (invalid declaration dropped, old-spec engines fall back to the default stretch/start alignment) with no error pointing at the mixin; the bogus `-ms-align-items` line shows the prefix list was assembled without per-property value checking, so the mixin's translation contract is already incomplete on the day it ships.

[BUG] The PR's only topic-post.scss changes — converting .small-action (a post-stream component, not the header) to flexbox and redesigning its spacing (padding '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' → '0 1.5%', margin-top: 5px removed, p margin 5px→0, padding-top: 4px removed) — have no traceable link to the stated 'header layout performance' intent. Reviewers approving a header performance change unknowingly sign off on a user-visible redesign of every small-action post row (system posts like topic closures/edits); the work cannot be evaluated against the stated requirement, and a later revert of the header work drags the unrelated post-stream restyle with it.

[ADVISORY] The new mixins emit vendor declarations for browser generations outside any plausible support matrix — display: -moz-box (2009-spec Firefox), -ms-flexbox (IE10), and -ms-align-items, a property no browser ever implemented — so every @include flexbox() ships 5 display declarations where 1 suffices. Compiled CSS grows by ~4 dead declarations per flexbox use, directly counter to the PR's performance framing; the prefix block also implies a legacy-browser support commitment no requirement asks for, and every future @include multiplies the bloat.

[ADVISORY] The badges.css.scss hunk is a computed-style no-op — it replaces 'display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline' with mixins that emit the identical standard declarations plus dead prefixes — and it is the sole consumer of the newly added inline-flex mixin. A performance-titled PR carries a zero-behavior-change refactor that expands its review surface; if this hunk is ever reverted, the inline-flex mixin it justifies becomes dead code permanently shipped in the stylesheet foundation.

[ADVISORY] The flexbox conversion lands in the shared common/base/header.scss, which also drives the mobile header, and the diff contains no mobile-scoped change, so mobile header layout changes as an unreviewed side effect — floats are ignored on flex items, so any float-based positioning assumptions for .title/.panel stop applying the moment .contents becomes a flex container. Mobile users receive an unreviewed layout-method swap in the header (panel pushed via margin-left:auto + order, children vertically centered via align-items); any mobile override relying on the old float behavior silently stops working and is only discovered after deploy.

[BUG] The new flexbox mixin emits display:-webkit-box/-moz-box, so 2009-spec-only engines (Android 4.1-4.3 stock browser, iOS 6 Safari) activate the old box model, where margin-left:auto on a flex item computes to 0 instead of absorbing free space - and margin-left:auto is now .panel's sole right-alignment mechanism after float:right was removed. On exactly the legacy engines the vendor prefixes are written to support, the header panel renders immediately after the title/extra-info-wrapper instead of at the right edge - a visible regression versus the float layout it replaces, which worked on those engines; the mixin abstraction advertises cross-spec flexbox support while the layout technique it lays out with is modern-spec-only.

[BUG] The align-items mixin emits -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align but no -moz-box-align, while its companion flexbox()/inline-flex() mixins emit display:-moz-box/-moz-inline-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group - so on Firefox builds whose newest supported display value is -moz-box (pre-Firefox 22), every @include align-items() in this diff resolves to no alignment declaration at all. Header .contents and .small-action lose their vertical centering and the .bullet category badge loses baseline alignment on those Firefox builds (items fall back to the engine default alignment) because the mixin family covers Gecko's old-spec display and ordering properties but not its alignment property - the registry is internally inconsistent across the spec generations it claims to span.

[ADVISORY] -ms-align-items is not a property any browser ever implemented (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, IE11+ uses unprefixed align-items), so the declaration is dead code documenting a fictional prefix mapping inside a mixin that presents itself as the authoritative cross-browser registry. No runtime effect, but the bogus entry signals the prefix list was copied without verification and will be trusted and copied into future mixins or theme overrides, propagating the error; it also masks the real omission in the same mixin (-moz-box-align).

[BUG] The diff strips all vertical spacing from small-action rows — .small-action-desc loses its 0.5em vertical padding and 5px margin-top, and its paragraphs lose margin 5px 0 (line 292) and padding-top 4px (dropped from the > p rule) — spacing edits that no flexbox conversion requires. Small-action text on every topic page renders flush against the rows' separator borders with collapsed vertical rhythm and a changed indent (4em fixed → 1.5% relative) — an unreviewed visual redesign of a non-header component shipped under a stated objective of 'header layout performance', i.e. the accepted intent silently drifted from behavior-preserving perf work to visual redesign.

[BUG] line-height: 1.5 is added to .extra-info-wrapper and .badge-wrapper.bullet's margin-top: 5px is deleted — visual edits to the topic-title meta line that the stated header-performance objective does not cover. The category badge and the title meta line shift vertically on every topic page without design sign-off; a reviewer who approved a header perf refactor unknowingly accepted a topic-page visual change.

[BUG] @include order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper compiles to inert declarations because the order property only applies to flex items and this diff establishes no flex formatting context on any ancestor of .extra-info-wrapper (flexbox() is applied only to .contents, .small-action and .badge-wrapper.bullet). The intended reordering silently does nothing — dead CSS in production, or evidence that a companion flex-container change was dropped between review iterations; a maintainer tuning the order value later sees no effect.

[BUG] Replacing .panel's float: right with margin-left: auto is not behavior-preserving on the 2009-spec tier the new mixins themselves emit first: in -webkit-box/-moz-box layout auto margins compute to 0, so the panel loses its right-edge alignment. On browsers that resolve display to -webkit-box/-moz-box (Android stock 2.3–4.3, Firefox ≤21, Safari ≤6) the header buttons render immediately after the site title instead of flush right — a regression on the very browsers the vendor-prefix mixins claim to support.

[ADVISORY] align-items(center) re-positions multi-line small-action descriptions from top-aligned (block flow beside the floated avatar) to vertically centered against the avatar, whereas flex-start would have preserved the previous alignment. Custom small-action messages taller than the avatar now hang at the vertical middle of the row — a rendering change inherent to the conversion choice that was never explicitly accepted as a design change.

[ADVISORY] The hand-maintained vendor matrix is already inconsistent and partly dead: align-items emits -webkit-box-align but omits -moz-box-align even though the flexbox mixin emits display: -moz-box (while order does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group), and -ms-align-items is a property no browser ever implemented. Legacy-Firefox-tier browsers get stretch alignment instead of the specified centering, and every future hand-added flex property risks repeating the omission; a build-time Autoprefixer step would delete all four mixins and this entire drift class with them.

[ADVISORY] The artifact does not deliver its stated objective: floats→flexbox is a layout modernization with no perf evidence, each converted rule grows by up to 15 vendor-prefixed declarations, and the diff simultaneously redesigns spacing in three non-header files. The change is reviewed and accepted under a performance framing that cannot be verified and will not materialize, providing cover for the unaccepted visual edits; future contributors will replicate the pattern expecting perf gains.

[ADVISORY] The new align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, a property no browser has ever implemented (IE's real property -ms-flex-align is already emitted one line above), and omits -moz-box-align even though the sibling flexbox() mixin emits display: -moz-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group. The hand-maintained prefix list is internally inconsistent the moment it lands: in the old-Firefox engines that display: -moz-box exists to serve, align-items: center/baseline silently falls back to the default stretch, misaligning the header contents, small-action rows, and bullet badges there, and every future caller of the mixin inherits the same silent gap; the -ms-align-items line is dead bytes shipped on every call site.

[BUG] Right-aligning .panel via margin-left: auto works only in modern-flexbox engines; in the 2009-box-model engines that the newly emitted display: -webkit-box/-moz-box values exist to serve, auto margins do not absorb free space, so after float: right is removed the panel is no longer pushed to the right edge. On engines that only implement the 2009 box spec (old WebKit including the Android <=4.3 stock browser, Firefox <=21), the search/avatar/menu panel renders immediately after the site title instead of right-aligned — a regression from the removed float in exactly the browsers the prefix layer claims to support; all supported browsers (IE11+, evergreen, Safari 7+ via -webkit-flex) are unaffected.

Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff strips all vertical spacing from small-action rows — .small-action-desc loses its 0.5em vertical padding and 5px margin-top, and its paragraphs lose margin 5px 0 (line 292) and padding-top 4px (dropped from the > p rule) — spacing edits that no flexbox conversion requires. Small-action text on every topic page renders flush against the rows' separator borders with collapsed vertical rhythm and a changed indent (4em fixed → 1.5% relative) — an unreviewed visual redesign of a non-header component shipped under a stated objective of 'header layout performance', i.e. the accepted intent silently drifted from behavior-preserving perf work to visual redesign.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove multiple vertical-spacing declarations in the `.small-action` component: `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%;` (no top/bottom padding and no margin-top), `.small-action-desc p` changes from `margin: 5px 0;` to `margin: 0;`, and `.small-action-desc > p` drops `padding-top: 4px;`. These are real, non-header visual/layout changes that go beyond the shown flexbox conversion itself, but the diff alone can’t prove they are a functional “bug” vs an intentional redesign.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] line-height: 1.5 is added to .extra-info-wrapper and .badge-wrapper.bullet's margin-top: 5px is deleted — visual edits to the topic-title meta line that the stated header-performance objective does not cover. The category badge and the title meta line shift vertically on every topic page without design sign-off; a reviewer who approved a header perf refactor unknowingly accepted a topic-page visual change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce topic-page visual/layout changes unrelated to the header refactor: `.extra-info-wrapper` gains `line-height: 1.5` and an `order(2)` mixin, and the nested `.badge-wrapper` loses the `&.bullet { margin-top: 5px; }` rule (topic.scss). These are verifiable from the diff and can shift vertical alignment/spacing of the topic title meta/badge line, but they are not a clear functional defect—more a scope/regression risk/design-change concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] @include order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper compiles to inert declarations because the order property only applies to flex items and this diff establishes no flex formatting context on any ancestor of .extra-info-wrapper (flexbox() is applied only to .contents, .small-action and .badge-wrapper.bullet). The intended reordering silently does nothing — dead CSS in production, or evidence that a companion flex-container change was dropped between review iterations; a maintainer tuning the order value later sees no effect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper`, and `order` only has effect when the element is a flex item. However, the diff does not show the CSS for `.extra-info-wrapper`’s parent/ancestor layout, so you cannot verify from this diff alone that it is *not already* inside a `display: flex` container elsewhere in the codebase. Therefore the claim that the declarations are definitely inert is not verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Replacing .panel's float: right with margin-left: auto is not behavior-preserving on the 2009-spec tier the new mixins themselves emit first: in -webkit-box/-moz-box layout auto margins compute to 0, so the panel loses its right-edge alignment. On browsers that resolve display to -webkit-box/-moz-box (Android stock 2.3–4.3, Firefox ≤21, Safari ≤6) the header buttons render immediately after the site title instead of flush right — a regression on the very browsers the vendor-prefix mixins claim to support.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.panel` switches from `float: right;` to `margin-left: auto;` and the container `.contents` becomes flex via `@include flexbox()`. The new `flexbox()` mixin emits legacy `display: -webkit-box;` / `display: -moz-box;` first. In those 2009-era flexbox implementations, auto margins generally don’t create the “push to right” behavior used in modern flexbox, so `.panel` may no longer align to the right edge and instead sit immediately after preceding content. This is a behavior change introduced by the diff and is tied directly to the vendor-prefixed modes the mixins enable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] align-items(center) re-positions multi-line small-action descriptions from top-aligned (block flow beside the floated avatar) to vertically centered against the avatar, whereas flex-start would have preserved the previous alignment. Custom small-action messages taller than the avatar now hang at the vertical middle of the row — a rendering change inherent to the conversion choice that was never explicitly accepted as a design change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.small-action` to a flex container and explicitly applies `@include align-items(center);` (topic-post.scss). In a row-style flex layout this will vertically center all direct children (e.g., the avatar and `.small-action-desc`) relative to each other, which is a real rendering change compared to the prior float/block-flow setup (previous `.small-action-desc` padding/margin-top suggest top-aligned text beside the avatar). Whether this is an intended design change isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the alignment shift called out is a concrete, diff-grounded UI behavior change worth reviewing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The hand-maintained vendor matrix is already inconsistent and partly dead: align-items emits -webkit-box-align but omits -moz-box-align even though the flexbox mixin emits display: -moz-box (while order does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group), and -ms-align-items is a property no browser ever implemented. Legacy-Firefox-tier browsers get stretch alignment instead of the specified centering, and every future hand-added flex property risks repeating the omission; a build-time Autoprefixer step would delete all four mixins and this entire drift class with them.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds hand-written flexbox vendor mixins in `mixins.scss`. `@mixin flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box;` and `@mixin order()` includes `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `@mixin align-items($alignment)` does not emit the corresponding `-moz-box-align`, creating an internal inconsistency that could affect old `-moz-box` implementations. The comment about `-ms-align-items` being nonstandard is also diff-grounded (it’s present in the mixin). While the exact runtime impact on specific legacy browsers isn’t verifiable from the diff alone, the maintainability/drift risk and missing `-moz-` counterpart are real and specific.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The artifact does not deliver its stated objective: floats→flexbox is a layout modernization with no perf evidence, each converted rule grows by up to 15 vendor-prefixed declarations, and the diff simultaneously redesigns spacing in three non-header files. The change is reviewed and accepted under a performance framing that cannot be verified and will not materialize, providing cover for the unaccepted visual edits; future contributors will replicate the pattern expecting perf gains.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does more than a simple floats→flexbox refactor: it adds new flexbox mixins with multiple vendor-prefixed declarations (mixins.scss: flexbox/inline-flex/align-items/order) and applies them in several places, which will expand CSS output substantially compared to the prior single `float` declarations. It also changes spacing/visual layout in non-header files (topic-post.scss: `.small-action-desc` padding/margins and paragraph margins; topic.scss: removes `.badge-wrapper.bullet` margin-top and adds `order(2)`/line-height; badges.css.scss: switches to mixins). The finding’s claims about “performance framing” and review intent aren’t verifiable from the diff, but the scope creep and CSS bloat concerns are diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, a property no browser has ever implemented (IE's real property -ms-flex-align is already emitted one line above), and omits -moz-box-align even though the sibling flexbox() mixin emits display: -moz-box and order() emits -moz-box-ordinal-group. The hand-maintained prefix list is internally inconsistent the moment it lands: in the old-Firefox engines that display: -moz-box exists to serve, align-items: center/baseline silently falls back to the default stretch, misaligning the header contents, small-action rows, and bullet badges there, and every future caller of the mixin inherits the same silent gap; the -ms-align-items line is dead bytes shipped on every call site.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `align-items($alignment)` mixin that emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but it does not emit `-moz-box-align`. This is inconsistent with the newly added `flexbox()` mixin emitting `display: -moz-box` and `order()` emitting `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, meaning callers using `@include flexbox(); @include align-items(...)` would not set the corresponding alignment property for the `-moz-box` model. The finding’s point that `-ms-align-items` is unnecessary is also consistent with the mixin already emitting `-ms-flex-align` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Right-aligning .panel via margin-left: auto works only in modern-flexbox engines; in the 2009-box-model engines that the newly emitted display: -webkit-box/-moz-box values exist to serve, auto margins do not absorb free space, so after float: right is removed the panel is no longer pushed to the right edge. On engines that only implement the 2009 box spec (old WebKit including the Android <=4.3 stock browser, Firefox <=21), the search/avatar/menu panel renders immediately after the site title instead of right-aligned — a regression from the removed float in exactly the browsers the prefix layer claims to support; all supported browsers (IE11+, evergreen, Safari 7+ via -webkit-flex) are unaffected.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` switches from floats to `@include flexbox()` and `.panel` drops `float: right` in favor of `margin-left: auto`. The new `flexbox()` mixin emits legacy 2009 `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` as well as modern flex values, but no corresponding legacy alignment (`-webkit-box-pack` / `-moz-box-pack`) is set. Auto margins are not a reliable/standard way to absorb free space in the 2009 box model, so in engines that pick `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` the panel may no longer be pushed to the right, making this a regression relative to the removed float.
